rationale: Ground truth has no substantive concerns (just Codex quota noise and 'thanks'), so recall is vacuous for both. X offers a mostly PASS scan plus one speculative, hedged nit (sm_110a) that isn't grounded in the shown diff and X admits is 'almost certainly fine.' Y does deeper repo-wide verification (greps for stale symbol names, cross-checks pyproject.toml and the doc's heading/table against the new datacenter-only scope) and surfaces multiple concrete, file:line, propose-the-exact-fix findings (stale 'SM 100+' table row, stale pyproject description, stale doc heading, and a sharper (major,minor) whitelist suggestion backed by a precedent in platform.py) that are actionable and plausible, though the e2e-verification-artifact ask is more process nag than code finding. Y is more thorough and grounded overall.
